name: Link
whenToUse: Going somewhere: another page, a section, a document, an external site.
Inside a sentence (no `size`, so it takes the text’s size) or as a standalone line with `size`.

whenNotToUse.text: Doing something: save, delete, open a dialog
A navigation item in a menu or sidebar
A whole card that leads somewhere

anatomy.description: says where it goes: “Billing settings”, not “click here”. `size` xs–lg, or inherited.
on hover by default; always with `underline`, thicker on hover.

do.caption: In running text the link is underlined, so it doesn’t rely on color alone.
do.example: Read the refund policy before you cancel.

dont.caption: Without the underline the link is just a blue word to anyone who can’t tell the colors apart.
dont.example: Read the refund policy before you cancel.

do.caption: An action is a Button, even a quiet one.

dont.caption: A link that deletes: screen readers announce “link”, and people expect it to navigate.

a11y: The text says where the link goes; “here”, “more” and “link” don’t make sense read out of context in a links list.
On a dark or primary surface use `inverse`: the default link color and focus ring don’t have the contrast there.
A link that opens a new tab says so in its text, e.g. “Pricing (opens in a new tab)”.
